problems.stem: A student writes the resume bullet: "Responsible for the social media of the robotics club." Which revision turns it into employer-ready evidence?
options: Helped out with the robotics club's social media accounts.
Grew the robotics club Instagram from 80 to 240 followers in one semester by posting a weekly build update.
Passionate and detail-oriented social media manager for robotics.
Responsible for managing all robotics club online presence and branding.
problems.explanation: A strong bullet pairs an action verb with a measurable, verifiable result (80 to 240 followers, one semester). The others restate the duty or add adjectives without evidence.

problems.stem: Your resume lists "Expert in Python" but you have only finished one intro CAT 100 module that used short scripts. What is the most defensible fix?
options: Leave it as "Expert in Python" because it sounds stronger to recruiters.
Change it to "Familiar with Python (intro coursework: wrote short data-cleaning scripts in CAT 100)."
Delete every mention of Python so nothing can be questioned.
Change it to "Advanced Python developer with production experience."
problems.explanation: Truthful evidence means the claim matches what you can show. Naming the level (familiar) and the source (intro coursework) is defensible; inflating to expert or advanced is not.

problems.stem: You ask an AI tool to tighten your resume bullets. It rewrites one as "Led a 12-person engineering team." You were one of 12 members, not the lead. What belongs in your AI-use note and final resume?
options: Accept the bullet as written; the AI is usually correct about phrasing.
Reject that suggestion, record it as rejected in the AI-use note, and keep a truthful bullet such as "Contributed as one of 12 members of the engineering build team."
Keep the AI bullet but add an emoji so it looks original.
Remove all AI involvement and do not mention that AI helped at all.
problems.explanation: AI is a bounded helper. You must reject claims that are untrue, log the decision in the AI-use note, and keep the surviving bullet verifiable.

problems.stem: You are applying to a data-entry internship that lists "Excel" and "attention to detail" as top requirements. Your resume leads with a graphic-design club bullet. What is the best role-fit revision?
options: Send the same resume; reordering is not worth the effort.
Move your Excel and data-accuracy bullets to the top so the most role-relevant evidence appears first, then keep design lower.
Delete every bullet that is not about Excel.
Add the word "Excel" five times so the keyword scanner ranks you higher.
problems.explanation: Role fit means ordering and keywords match the posting. Lead with the most relevant verifiable evidence; do not delete real experience or keyword-stuff.
